replacements.before:

Table~\ref{tab:process-summary} reports output size, delegated invocations, goal events, token accounting, and wall-clock time across the three generation runs.
For \condAgenticCogWriter, the three run-level summaries average \AfourOutputTokensMean\ output-plus-reasoning tokens and \AfourInputTokensMean\ uncached input tokens per attempted run, while accepted goal regeneration averages \AfourGoalRegeneratedMean\ events.

replacements.instruction: Replace the run-1-only output-length sensitivity narrative with per-run reporting over all three generation runs. Keep the runs separate because the same prompt set is regenerated and the runs are not independent replications.
replacements.before:
Table~\ref{tab:appendix-length-control} reports pairwise outcomes by output-length ratio.
The longer side wins \LengthLongerRate\ of \LengthLongerNonTie\ non-tied comparisons.
In the tighter pre-specified matching band, the outcomes from the first generation run for our system are \LengthFullSinglePassFiveWLT\ versus \condSinglePass\ ($p=\LengthFullSinglePassFiveP$), \LengthFullTaskPlanningFiveWLT\ versus \condTaskPlanning\ ($p=\LengthFullTaskPlanningFiveP$), and \LengthFullNoGoalsFiveWLT\ versus \condNoGoals.
In the wider pre-specified band, the corresponding outcomes are \LengthFullSinglePassTenWLT\ ($p=\LengthFullSinglePassTenP$), \LengthFullTaskPlanningTenWLT\ ($p=\LengthFullTaskPlanningTenP$), and \LengthFullNoGoalsTenWLT\ ($p=\LengthFullNoGoalsTenP$).
These matching-band $p$-values are unadjusted descriptive sign-test results.
replacements.after:
Table~\ref{tab:appendix-length-control} reports pre-specified output-length-matched win rates for our system separately for all three generation runs.
Within each run and comparison, we retain pairs at or below the stated output-length ratio, apply the two-order consistency rule, and compute $W/(W+L)$ after excluding ties.
Keeping the runs separate respects the shared prompt set rather than treating the three generation runs as independent replications.

replacements.instruction: Replace the run-1 process/resource table body with existing three-run mean macros for the run-level summaries and remove the run-1 completion column, so the table matches the study scope instead of selectively displaying the first run.
replacements.before: \caption{Realized process and resource use in generation run 1 of 3. The systems differ substantially in delegated invocations and token use in addition to their control logic, while accepted goal regeneration is rare. These realized differences motivate the output-length and compute-matched sensitivity analyses rather than treating raw resource use as a controlled mechanism.}
replacements.after: \caption{Process and resource use across the three generation runs. Each value is the mean of the three run-level summaries; Median units therefore averages the run-level medians rather than recomputing a median after joining runs. Goal entries report mean created/developed/regenerated events. These realized differences motivate the output-length and compute-matched sensitivity analyses rather than treating raw resource use as a controlled mechanism.}

replacements.instruction: Replace the run-1 output-length-ratio table with existing matched-band win-rate macros for runs 1, 2, and 3, so the sensitivity analysis exposes every available pre-specified generation run without treating runs as independent observations.
replacements.before: \caption{Pairwise outcomes from generation run 1 of 3 grouped by output-length ratio. Longer responses are favored overall, motivating the matched-length checks used to test whether the main system comparisons survive when output lengths are more similar. Here, W/L/T denotes wins/losses/ties for the longer response after applying the two-order consistency rule; ties are excluded from the longer-side win-rate denominator.}
replacements.after: \caption{Output-length-matched win rates for our system in each generation run. Rows retain pairs whose output-length ratio is at most the stated threshold, and each rate is $W/(W+L)$ within that run after the two-order consistency rule; ties are excluded. Reporting runs separately keeps the shared prompt set from being treated as independent replication.}
